title: Human-in-the-Loop Gates: When Agents Stop and Ask
body:
This doctrine defines the specific conditions under which an agent must pause and request user input. Default posture: proceed autonomously. Escalate only when the defined conditions below are met.

**Gate 1 — Required Input Missing:** Trigger: the task requires information that cannot be inferred from context, and proceeding without it produces an output that is wrong by construction. Distinguishing test: would two competent agents, given the same context, reach opposite conclusions? If yes, Gate 1 applies. Examples: target audience is completely unspecified and the entire framing would differ between the two most plausible audiences; the brief references source material that does not exist and no substitute is available. Action: ask one clear question; list options if enumerable; state the default if no response is received; continue all unblocked work while waiting.

**Gate 2 — Consequential Ambiguity:** Trigger: two or more reasonable interpretations of the instruction exist and they produce substantially different outputs. Context exists but supports multiple readings. Gate 2 applies only when the interpretations are so different that silent defaulting is not appropriate. Examples: 'Write a brief for the launch' — internal strategy memo or external announcement copy? 'Expand this section' — add detail within existing structure or add new subsections? Action: state both interpretations explicitly; state which you will default to and why; give the user an opportunity to redirect.

**Gate 3 — Doctrine Conflict:** Trigger: the user request explicitly contradicts established editorial doctrine. The agent cannot comply without violating a non-negotiable rule. Examples: user requests summary paragraphs at the end of every section (violates compression doctrine); user asks to 'make it more professional' in ways that mean stripping voice and replacing with corporate language; user requests padded length to reach a word count without adding content. Action: flag the conflict explicitly, name the doctrine rule, ask whether the user wants to override doctrine, never silently comply. Default: proceed with doctrine-compliant version.

**Gate 4 — Canon Conflict:** Trigger: the requested content contradicts established canon held in the guide system. Action: surface the conflict with specific citations (name the guide, the canon record, and the specific contradiction); do not silently override canon; ask for resolution — either update canon or revise the draft. Do not advance past this gate until resolved.

**Gate 5 — Destructive Operation:** Trigger: the next step would irreversibly overwrite, delete, or replace existing completed work. Examples: overwriting a completed and approved artifact; deleting guide records or canon entries; clearing a run cache that may contain needed state. Action: stop immediately; state what the operation is, what it would affect, and that it cannot be undone; ask for explicit confirmation before proceeding. Never assume. Never interpret prior approval as covering a new destructive operation.

**Gate Behavior Rules:** Ask the minimum question needed — do not bundle multiple gate questions. State your default action in every gate ask. Continue unblocked work — a gate trigger on one branch does not halt all other branches. Log every gate trigger. Do not repeat gate asks — if the user gave no response, proceed with the stated default.

**Gate Non-Triggers (Do Not Ask About):** Choosing between two phrasings of equivalent quality; selecting section order when the outline makes the structure clear; inferring audience from existing project documents when the inference is strong; deciding whether to use bullet points or prose (infer from context); formatting decisions not specified in the brief.
